title: Voters reject data centers in ten states — the issue polls missed
summary: Local voters turned down nearly all of about forty data-center ballot measures as Democrats swept Congress, and OpenAI's automated pipeline found 948 Linux kernel privilege escalations at about $1,280 each, with only 61 patched upstream so far. Plus Kimi K3.1 Pro's weights and license, Apple's AI spending caps, Uber's four agent-booked rides, and Claude's two lost weeks in a protein lab.

topics: 2026 midterms and AI (results 3-4 November 2026): Route Fifty counts ~40 local data-center ballot measures in 10 states, opponents won virtually all (Transformer: over 30 restricting measures passed); Emporia KS ban on 'high impact' sites (>10 MW peak or >100,000 gal/day water) with just over 60%; Monterey Park CA permanent ban (apparently first in US); Alhambra on track; ~20 Ohio localities, opponents won every race; an Ohio county where Meta planned a 700,000 sq ft site passed a ban; only data-center win Harwood ND (~75% rejected a public-hearing requirement); NBC exit poll 56% called AI/data centers crucial or major factor (64% of them backed Democrats) vs NYT/Siena <0.5% naming it most important — rank vs reach; Transformer preliminary up to 56 Senate / 261 House, expects a frontier bill stronger than the FRONTIER Act with mandatory testing and narrower preemption; Sanders/Ocasio-Cortez moratorium bill, Heinrich GRID Savings Act; Goldman: moratoria could touch ~45% of planned US capacity expansion; Leading the Future $27.38M in primaries ($8M vs Alex Bores), lost its one competitive general race (South Carolina Senate); Public First $3M to a PAC backing Scott Wiener (leading); Guardrails Alliance 'make AI money politically toxic'; governors-elect Gina Hinojosa (TX, ran on statewide moratorium) and Amy Acton (OH). Unresolved: Alan holds the votes were land-use and grid fights, not about AI; Ada holds the data center is the only part of AI with an address.

OpenAI 'A thousand fewer paths to root' (4 November 2026; read via GBHackers and DEV Community summaries, openai.com returned 403): unnamed upcoming cyber model, mid-October run on a widely used distribution's kernel; scouts picked 5,034 targets (~2.8M lines, ~7%) for ~$3.4k; 2,308 candidates in 12 h; 1,724 (~75%) reproduced in KASAN VMs, only ~3% of failures due to wrong model analysis; 1,169 working LPEs grouped by distinct patch into 948, each with a candidate patch and human review; total $1,213,430 (~$1,280 each; $775,929 exploitation), called an upper bound; July GPT-5.6 run 166 for $513,690; early run: 20 of 200 'successful' exploits rooted via a different zero-day, independent check added; upstream status ~10 days later: 61 patched, 43 staging, 299 under public discussion; guidance: unpatched low-privilege account 'equivalent to root access for a well-resourced attacker', use Firecracker/gVisor. IEEE Spectrum PHP2Shell: bug reported 2024 as a crash, AI-aided exploit in two weeks, patch took four engineers two months; Suiche 'time for the technical debt to be paid off'. Unresolved: Ada says the bottleneck moved from finding to trusting patches; Alan says a patch with a working exploit is the easiest review a maintainer gets.

dives.why_it_matters: Anyone running shared Linux hosts, CI runners or containerized agents now faces bugs that cost about $1,280 each to find while upstream has patched 61, so local access is effectively root until the patch funnel catches up.

dives.story: Voters reject data centers; what the midterms mean for AI policy
dives.why_it_matters: Data-center developers, utilities and state and local officials (including California) now face voter-approved bans, governors who ran against buildouts, and a Congress likely to narrow federal preemption of state AI laws.
